findings.title: Migration crashes with NoMethodError when embed_category is unset or doesn't match a category
findings.body: The migration looks up the old `embed_category` site setting via `execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories AS c INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i`. On any install where the `embed_category` setting is empty (its default is '') or its value doesn't match a category name, the query returns zero rows, so `[0]` is nil and `nil['id']` raises NoMethodError, aborting the migration. The `if category_id == 0` fallback on line 14 was clearly meant to handle the 'not found' case, but it is unreachable because the code crashes before it. The lookup must tolerate an empty result set (e.g. `rows[0].try(:[], 'id').to_i`) before the fallback can work.

findings.title: Migrated host values are inserted verbatim (no scheme/path stripping) and interpolated raw into SQL
findings.body: The migration takes each line of the old `embeddable_hosts` site setting and inserts it directly via raw SQL. The old setting accepted values like `http://discourse.org` or `https://example.com/1234` (the PR's own controller spec fabricates exactly such values), but `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` matches with `lower(host) = uri.host` (e.g. 'discourse.org'). Because the INSERT bypasses the model's `before_validation` callbacks that strip the scheme and path, any migrated host containing a protocol prefix or path will never match a referer, silently breaking embedding for those sites after upgrade. Additionally, the value is interpolated into the SQL string with `#{h}`; a value containing a single quote (possible in the free-text setting) breaks the SQL statement. The migration should normalize each host the same way the model does and use quoted/parameterized values.

findings.title: update/destroy raise NoMethodError (500) when the host id doesn't exist or params are missing
findings.body: In `update` and `destroy`, `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` returns nil for an unknown id; `save_host(nil)` then does `host.host = ...` on nil, and `destroy` calls `nil.destroy`, both producing a 500 instead of a 404. Similarly, `save_host` dereferences `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` without checking the param exists, and if `host` is assigned nil the model's `before_validation` block (`self.host.sub!`) raises NoMethodError instead of returning a validation error. Stale ids (e.g. the record deleted in another tab) will surface as server errors rather than a clean error response.

findings.title: Category and embeddable_host fabricator contents are swapped between files
findings.body: This PR puts the `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)` definition into `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` (whose entire category content was deleted) and moves all the category fabricators (`:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category`, `:private_category`) into the newly added `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb`. Tests still pass because Fabricator loads all files, but the file names no longer reflect their contents at all; anyone adding or editing a category fabricator will look in the wrong file, and this is clearly an accidental file mix-up rather than an intentional move. The contents should be swapped back so each fabricator lives in its matching file.

findings.title: EmbeddingController#update is a no-op that reports success without saving anything
findings.body: The `update` action (routed via `put "customize/embedding"`) fetches the embedding data and re-renders it, but never applies any submitted attributes. The admin controller's `saveChanges` action calls `this.get('embedding').update({})` against this endpoint, so a client saving changes gets a 200 with the unchanged payload while any data is silently discarded. Either the action should process and persist the submitted parameters, or the route/action and the client `saveChanges` code should be removed so nobody is led to believe saving works.

findings.title: New admin controllers have no behavioral tests (create/update/destroy, validation, permissions)
findings.body: Both `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` and `Admin::EmbeddingController` specs only assert that the class is a subclass of `Admin::AdminController`. There is no test covering create/update/destroy of embeddable hosts, the host normalization/validation rules, the category_id fallback to uncategorized, error rendering for invalid hosts, or access control (e.g. that a non-admin is rejected). Given this controller writes data that gates which external sites can embed content, at least CRUD and authorization request specs should be added; as written, the nil-id and bad-param failures described elsewhere would not be caught.

findings.title: create_table uses force: true in a production migration
findings.body: `create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true` will drop the table (and all host/category data) if it already exists when the migration runs. Using `force: true` is appropriate in schema definitions for test convenience, not in a shipped migration; if the table pre-exists on any install (e.g. from a partially applied migration or a plugin), this migration silently destroys the data instead of failing loudly.
